recipes.name: Chicken and Red Wine Sauce
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook garlic in oil until tender.

Place chicken in the skillet, and cook for about 10 minutes on each side, until no longer pink and juices run clear. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Drain oil from the skillet. Sprinkle chicken with paprika and brown sugar.
Pour red wine around chicken. Cover and simmer, 15 to 20 minutes; lightly baste the chicken with wine sauce while cooking. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Red Wine Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This chicken and red wine recipe has balanced flavor from brown sugar, garlic, and paprika. Enjoy this simple, comforting dish with a delicious sauce.

review.reviewBody: I adjusted this recipe slghtly after reading the other reviews. It must have worked because my husband, who belongs to "picky-eaters anonomous" asked for seconds! This recipe makes the best chicken I have ever tasted. The adjustemnts I made were to decrease the paprkia and brown sugar by half, only use 3/4 c wine and leave the lid off so it thickens better. Try it, you'll love it!

Following some of the advice of others, I modified this recipe to tailor it to my family's tastes.
For this, I used four boneless chicken breasts with the tenderloin cut to create eight pieces of chicken. I added sliced onions and mushrooms, which I sauted before browning the chicken and returned to the pot after adding the liquid. I also cut back the sugar to 1/4 cup, as per others suggestions.
In addition, I only used 1/2 cup of a nice "Concho y Toro" chilean merlot and added 1/2 cup of reduced sodium chicken broth for the liquid.
I dredged the chicken in seasoned salt and the paprika and let it sit 15 minutes which helped to create a nice color during the browning process, as I decided not to fully cook the chicken before the simmer to reduce dryness.
I also thickened the broth, as per a suggestion, after removing the cooked chicken by adding 1 tablespoon cornstarch and heating to boiling.
This recipe was excellent! My two year old gobbled up the chicken and demanded not only seconds but thirds! The sauce, thick with onions and mushrooms, made a wonderful gravy for mashed potatoes. 
I was paid the highest compliment for this dish as my mother-in-law asked for the recipe! What better endorsement than that? Enjoy!

This recipe was great, but the measurements on the ingredient list must be way off. 1 1/2 cups of sugar is WAY too much. So is 1 tablespoon of salt. This recipe is perfect with about 1/2 cup of sugar, 1 teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of pepper and t teaspoon of paprika. Also, I suggest simmering the chicken with the lid off so the wine will reduce a bit.

This is a wonderful recipe! I used skinned, boneless thighs instead of breasts. Sauteed about one tablespoon garlic, red onion, and some mushrooms before cooking the chicken. Set that aside and put back in after the wine was added. I added fresh ground pepper, and salted the thighs with a little kosher salt. Also used about 1/2 cup brown sugar sprinkled on both sides with the tablespoon of paprika. Added about 1 tablespoon of cornstarch to the wine to thicken the sauce. I also added about half a tablespoon of garlic salt. Decided not to drain the drippings as I thought it would give it more flavor. Awesome! Husband just LOVED it!

I had to make some changes. Like many others, I sautéed onion and fresh mushrooms with the garlic. Removed from pan and then seared the chicken, which I put the paprika and salt on. I then used 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chicken broth, and 1/2 cup red wine and simmered the chicken and veggies for 30 minutes. I then thickened using some chicken broth and 1 tablespoon of flour. Delicious. Will make again.

Pleasantly surprised! I love dishes with wine, especially red wine. After reading the other reviews, I only used 1/4 cup of brown sugar and 1/2 a teaspoon of paprika, along with my cup of Cabernet wine. The other change I made, I used chicken thighs instead of breasts. I’m not sure what I did different than others but even tho I covered the skillet, after 10 minutes of simmering I had to add more wine and decided to add about 1/2 cup of chicken broth too. At the 20 minute mark, my chicken had a super thick glaze, so I removed it from the heat while I finished making mashed cauliflower (instead of carby mashed potatoes) and asparagus. I told my husband that he probably wasn’t going to like the chicken because he doesn’t care for sweet meals (and it was sweet!) but he loved it and actually had seconds.

This is a really different recipe, easy and delicious. I altered the recipe by first marinating chicken thighs in Soy Vay Island Teriyaki marinade (Kroger) for about a half hour.? I only used about a quarter cup of the brown sugar, half a cup of wine and reduced with cover off due to the extra marinade liquid.? I only used about 1/4 cup of the brown sugar, 1/2 cup of wine and reduced with cover off due to the extra marinade liquid. I topped with chopped fresh green onions to serve.

I’m only giving it 3 stars since it seems the actual recipe is not great. I followed other people’s suggestions (half the sugar) and it was great! Another reviewer suggested sautéed veggies with it and I did the same with onions and bell peppers. I also didn’t cook the chicken breasts fully because it would have been really dry so I did 5 minutes each side then the simmering, it ended at 155 degrees Internal temperature and was very moist and juicy. (It is a-ok to eat chicken that’s not 165 degrees depending on how long you have been cooking the chicken). All in all, the ingredients for this recipe worked well! Just half the sugar!

Love. loVe.LOVE! The whole family loved it including the seven and three year old!. Lots of paprika for color. Sauteed garlic and onions before adding chicken to brown. Added rosemary, basil and parsley on top of chicken along with seasoning salt. One cup of red wine to half cup of brown sugar which was could still be cut diwn slightly. A dash of soy and bam! I left the lid off during simmer as well to reduce sauce. Served it over butter garlic noddles with slivers of carrot twisted in and fresh green beans. One of my favorite recipes on here so far!!! Oh and cant forget i let the chicken marinate in the wine in the fridge while i chopped, boiled and diced...

This was absolutely delicious! After reading some of the comments and based on my own tastes, I tweaked it just a little: I used 1-1/2 cups of red wine and 1/2 cup of low-sodium chicken broth (to make more sauce) and then thickened it with a little cornstarch and water once the chicken was done; used the full cup of brown sugar but didn't pack it into the measuring cup; and only browned the chicken breasts on both sides before adding the sauce ingredients, then cooked them thoroughly. I didn't feel the paprika added much to the flavor profile at all; next time I might add some grated ginger instead.

WOW WOW WOW! Tonight I made this delicious dish, I added mushrooms and for a side some oven roasted potatoes. So much flavor and the chicken is super tender. The only thing I did differently was cover with a lid and put it in the oven for 20 minutes and basted twice. Definitely will make again.
Turned out great, use half the sugar.

I made this for my picky eating wife and son. They loved it. They said not to cut back on the sugar so much next time. (I used less than a fourth of a cup.) I am making it as I type this with more sugar this time! Thanks for the recipe!

I followed the instructions , cooking the chicken for 10 minutes each side , then pouring the wine over the chicken and simmering for 10 minutes more. The chicken was so tough and dry, we could not eat it! All I can think of is that I cut the chicken too thin ( I wasn't sure what a chicken breast half was) and I used too big a pan so the simmering wine didn't cover the chicken.
Is it normal for the chicken to turn purple? The taste was good but unsure if I'll make again.Might try a different red.

It was okay. My son seemed to really like it though. Definitely way too much brown sugar, so I would cut that in half. I would add the garlic to the sauce because it burned while the chicken was cooking.
Easy to follow far too sweet. I only used three quarters of the sugar and it was still too much. I will try it again with greatly reduced sugar. Even half as much may still be very sweet.

Next time I will use less brown sugar. If you cook the chicken slowly, the garlic won’t burn. I used the cup of red wine but took chicken out and reduced the wine with a slow boil and no lid. My kids loved it. Served with rice and vegetables. Yum!
This turned out very well. Everyone enjoyed it.

It's quite easy and delicious! I did heed other reviews and added only half the sugar and mixed all the spices with the sugar before adding them to the chicken. However, I still found it too sweet. Next time I'll be adding only 1/4 cup of sugar.
